evals.name: settings-page-styling
evals.prompt: I need to build a new settings page for the app — make it look right
evals.expected_output: A complete React component using the design system constants (SPACING, SEMANTIC_COLORS, TYPOGRAPHY, TRANSITIONS), Card component, focus indicators, and dark-theme-appropriate styling

assertions.text: Imports and uses SPACING or SPACING_PATTERNS from @/config/spacing instead of arbitrary pixel values
Uses the Card component from @/components/ui/Card instead of raw Box with inline card styling
Includes _focus or FOCUS_STYLES on interactive elements for accessibility
No white or light backgrounds; uses dark bg values consistent with the brand (rgba dark or #091326)

evals.name: alert-banner-colors
evals.prompt: What colors should I use for a new alert banner that shows when gas fees are high?
evals.expected_output: A response recommending semantic colors (warning=#fbbf24, danger=#ef4444), a React component with glow effects and standard transitions, dark-appropriate backgrounds, and explanation of color rationale

assertions.text: Uses #fbbf24 (yellow) or SEMANTIC_COLORS.warning for the warning/elevated state
Uses #ef4444 (red) or SEMANTIC_COLORS.danger for the danger/very-high state
Includes glow or shadow effects (box-shadow with rgba glow pattern)
Imports from config/transitions rather than using inline transition strings
Uses dark transparent backgrounds (rgba dark values or matching card BG pattern)
The response explains WHY specific colors were chosen in brand context, not just what they are

evals.name: ditto-liquidation-message
evals.prompt: I'm adding a new Ditto message for when a user's collateral is close to liquidation — how should it look and what should it say?
evals.expected_output: A response identifying ALERT type with danger severity, voice-compliant message text (1-3 lines, no greetings/emojis), cooldown rules, DittoMessage contract object, and threshold-based triggers

assertions.text: Identifies ALERT as the message type since liquidation risk is a safety/blocking concern
Uses danger severity level for near-liquidation scenarios
Message text is 1-3 lines, no greetings, no emojis, implication-oriented (explains what it means, not just what it is)
Specifies cooldown or anti-annoyance rules (e.g., cooldownSec, frequency limits)
Provides a DittoMessage object matching the contract interface (id, type, severity, body, when, cooldownSec, showAs)
Defines numeric threshold conditions for when to trigger (e.g., riskScore >= 85)
